gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Apple's own tech specs cap the M1 MacBook Air at one external display, and the M3 MacBook Air at one with the lid open, so a driver-free two-screen extender can light only one of its screens beside the MacBook's own display.
standout_why: I opened five of the results: theofficejournal.com under-150 and attachable guides, dejaflow.com, twelvetabs.com and deal.ai. All stop at 'the USB-C port must carry video (DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt), otherwise HDMI plus a USB power cable'; dejaflow and twelvetabs add that one model needs a DisplayLink driver. None names a MacBook display limit or says each added screen uses up one of the laptop's display outputs. ChatGPT's second answer only gestures at 'MacBooks with external display limitations' without a number or a source. deskfinds.com returned HTTP 403, so it is not compared.
decides: It splits the pick by laptop, provided the page first sources each row's video path. For a shopper on an M1 MacBook Air, or an M3 Air with the lid open, a single added screen is the only kind that works without a driver. A driver-free two-screen extender such as the FOPO S1 would only pay off on a laptop that drives two external displays, on Apple's figures. That reading of the S1 is my inference from the 'driver-free' label in Dealectric's record: the FOPO store returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today, so its video path is not confirmed from its own page. The Mobile Pixels Fold's video path could not be read either (also HTTP 429).

findings.label: External displays an M1 MacBook Air drives (Apple)
findings.value: 1 external display, up to 6K at 60 Hz, alongside the built-in display
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (M1, 2020) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's Display Support section: 'Simultaneously supports full native resolution on the built-in display at millions of colors and: One external display with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz'.

findings.label: Video path on an M1 MacBook Air's USB-C ports (Apple)
findings.value: Native DisplayPort output over USB-C; Thunderbolt 3 digital video output
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (M1, 2020) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: This is the native (no-driver) path a 'driver-free' USB-C screen relies on.

findings.label: External displays an M3 MacBook Air drives (Apple)
findings.value: 1 external display up to 6K at 60 Hz with the lid open; a second, up to 5K at 60 Hz, only with the lid closed
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (13-inch, M3, 2024) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple: 'Close the MacBook Air lid to use a second external display with up to 5K resolution at 60Hz'. An extender mounted on the lid cannot be used with the lid closed; that last step is my inference, not Apple's wording.

findings.label: Named reviewer on the base-chip MacBook limit
findings.value: "the plain M1/M2 MacBooks support just one extra screen"
findings.source_title: CopGain Dual Laptop Screen Extender review: Portability with a very specific purpose (Simon Jary, Macworld, May 3, 2023)
findings.note: Jary tested on a 14-inch MacBook Pro. The review does not say how a dual extender behaves on a base M1/M2 and does not mention drivers.

findings.label: What the top-ranked rival says about the video path
findings.value: "Single-cable use needs a USB-C port with video output (DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt)"; otherwise "you'll typically need HDMI plus a separate USB cable for power"
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extenders Under $150 (2026) | The Office Journal
findings.note: No MacBook display limit, no driver, no cable or port count for two-screen models, no wattage. The page says it is based on published specifications, not hands-on testing.

findings.label: What the other opened rivals say
findings.value: dejaflow: SideTrak Slide "Needs DisplayLink driver install". twelvetabs: Upperizon dual "A DisplayLink driver must be installed, per its listing", and a buyer review that "running both screens takes three ports on the laptop". deal.ai: "triple-screen models need USB-C or HDMI plus power"
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extenders on Amazon (2026)
findings.note: dejaflow read at https://dejaflow.com/blog/2026/02/16/laptop-screen-extenders-under-150/ and deal.ai at https://deal.ai/best/best-laptop-screen-extenders, both 2026-11-21. None mentions an M1/M2/M3 display limit or MST.
